news.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
paras: NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter, both older than planned, are not doing science on Mars. Perseverance is in safe mode because one of its two UHF radios failed, so it switches to a weaker backup. That weaker radio can only send small data directly to Earth at X‑band speeds.
Odyssey, launched in 2001, has been orbiting Mars longer than any other mission, but now it also pauses. NASA teams are testing the backup radio’s power and determining why the main link stopped.

sport.title: November 25, 1999: The day Agassi was crowned year-end world No 1, two years after dropping out of the top 100
paras: On this day, November 25, 1999, Andre Agassi beat Gustavo Kuerten in straight sets to secure the year-end world No 1 ranking On this day, November 25, 1999, Andre Agassi defeated Gustavo Kuerten in the last round-robin match of the ATP Tour World Championships (6-4, 7-5).

Hard to believe, considering that only two years before, Agassi had dropped down to world No 141 before making his way back to the top. Andre Agassi, the Las Vegas Kid, was also a tennis legend. This title was followed by the 1994 US Open and the 1995 Australian Open , the only time he beat his long-time rival, Pete Sampras, in a Grand Slam final (4-6, 6-1, 7-6, 6-4).

sport.title: Meet the player who won 36 consecutive matches at the Davis Cup and beat Bjorn Borg’s all-time record
paras: The 11-time Grand Slam champion compiled a 37-3 singles record at the international team event, winning 33 consecutive singles rubbers between 1973 and 1980. During the run, Borg led Sweden to their one and only Davis Cup title .

Around 46 years after Borg’s final Davis Cup match, his record of 33 straight match wins was eclipsed. Marcos Baghdatis, a finalist at the 2006 Australian Open, won his 34th consecutive Davis Cup singles rubber on March 4, 2017. The Cypriot star secured the record after defeating Andorran player Jean-Baptiste Poux-Gautier in Europe Zone Group III in Estonia.
